notes:
- Image layers: place a picture from a file or another photograph from the catalog over your photograph, and shape it with Transform, Skew, Perspective and Warp.
- New Layer via Copy (Cmd+J, Ctrl+J on Windows) lifts a selected subject onto its own layer, ready to move, transform or warp.
- Warp layers bend everything below them, and a mask on one warps just your subject. Bake Warp turns one into an image layer, and Unbake brings the live warp back.
- Photo > Flip mirrors the whole photograph with every edit on it, and Finish layers can be flipped and duplicated on their own.
- Gradient layers can color by tone, replacing the Gradient Map adjustment.
- A tidier Finish toolbar, and layer settings that open and close with a chevron.
- Turn a layer mask off and back on with Shift-click or Layer > Disable Layer Mask.
- To Mask and Mask from selection make an ordinary mask you can paint; Shift-click adds a selection to it and Option-click (Alt-click) takes one out.
- Polish solves fine edges such as fur at full resolution, and Select > Polish refines a Smart layer's mask directly.
- Option-click (Alt-click) a mask or depth eye to see it as a red overlay on the photograph.
- Curves and the histogram can show their channels as CMY ink, and a curve can be copied to another channel in Curves and Recolor.
- Preview a Relight or Recolor look on your own photograph before you apply it.
- Develop adjustment layers have an Opacity slider.
- Capture sharpening for RAW photographs, and 100 percent now shows one photograph pixel per screen pixel.
- Export a Develop section, the depth map or a layer's mask as its own layer in a TIFF or EXR.
- Node recipes: ready-made groups in the node palette, your own saved as editable recipe files, with controls you can publish on a group.
- Eleven advanced graph nodes, node menus split into sections, wires you can draw from either end, and Duplicate Nodes (Cmd+D, Ctrl+D on Windows).
- An optional assistant answers questions from the user guide with a model you run on your own computer or home network, and can walk you through the steps.
- Recovery bundles can keep baked pictures, and Edit > Forget Missing Trashed Photos tidies the catalog.
- On a small window or at a large App Zoom, the photograph keeps its room.
- Brush edges, textured brushes and the finest brushes look at Fit as they export.
- A warp that enlarges the picture stays sharp at Fit.
- Masks, strokes and selections stay on their subject when you crop again.
- Smart clicks and color pickers read what is under the pointer on a cropped, turned, lens-corrected or warped photograph.
- Heal and clone at 1:1, warps and masked Warp layers look as they export.
- Layers from File brings TIFF and EXR layers in at their true brightness, fitted instead of stretched.
- A selection that crosses itself keeps every part filled, and a thin ellipse keeps its edge.
- Sliders, the 1:1 view and runs of undo are faster.
- Undo takes back Reset All Edits.
- The middle mouse button always pans, whatever tool is in hand.
- Verify recovery bundle names what is actually wrong.
- Menus open where they fit at a large App Zoom, and the cursor readout keeps clear of the Take menu.
- Stack and panorama thumbnails match the viewer.
- Moving to another photograph puts the tool down and resets the tools' session settings.
